title: Dispatch: F-018 fell too; every fact on the record is now matched by meaningless text, one fact at a time
statement: R-017 reproduced F-018 (section vocabulary) with the drifting line chain, so each of the 17 established facts except F-019, which is new, has been met by text made without language, and F-001 is met only inside the R-008 generator. Read the R-017 method closely: its tables come from a window of public pages that slides through the book in manuscript order, so it carries the manuscript's own section vocabularies by its schedule; F-018 therefore says the word stock moves with the book, not that the text means anything, and a run with the schedule shuffled would show how much of the attack rests on that. The per-fact attacks have done their job; the test that can still tell us something is one fixed procedure against every fact at once (G-every-fact), and the drifting chain behind R-016 and R-017 should be sent there as it stands, before anyone tunes it further. Two facts to watch: F-019 (p and f words on paragraph first lines, first word set aside) is unattacked, and a pending code change adds Timm's own unit to the line-to-line test, where on practice pages words one glyph apart gather on the line above more than in any of 46 reference languages, while identical words do not (F-017). Anchors: four drafts have dissenting second looks waiting to merge and none is confirmed; the next anchor work should be a candidate-masked test of published herbal identifications (P-L4-001), not more single-page drafts.
check: None: a dispatch. Counts as on /desk/brief at the time of writing (2026-11-25): 17 facts established, 2 refuted, 15 attacks succeeded, 78 keys failed.
